[vc_row row_height_percent=”0″ override_padding=”yes” h_padding=”2″ top_padding=”3″ bottom_padding=”2″ overlay_alpha=”50″ gutter_size=”3″ column_width_percent=”100″ shift_y=”0″ z_index=”0″ content_parallax=”0″ uncode_shortcode_id=”277652″][vc_column width=”3/12″][/vc_column][vc_column column_width_percent=”100″ gutter_size=”4″ overlay_alpha=”50″ shift_x=”0″ shift_y=”0″ shift_y_down=”0″ z_index=”0″ medium_width=”0″ mobile_width=”0″ width=”6/12″ uncode_shortcode_id=”191092″][vc_row_inner][vc_column_inner width=”1/1″][vc_custom_heading uncode_shortcode_id=”294958″]Introduction[/vc_custom_heading][vc_column_text uncode_shortcode_id=”110448″]A good conversion rate leads to increased revenue without the need for additional traffic. The average Shopify store converts at 1.4%, and anything above 3.2% puts you in the top 20%. If you want the benchmarks first, here is what counts as a good conversion rate on Shopify. This guide is about the strategies that move your own number.

In this guide, we will explore actionable strategies to improve conversions and maximise your store’s success. I’m a Shopify Expert specialising in UX and conversion design, and below I’ll walk through the exact areas I focus on when auditing a store. I will highlight a recent success story of Shopify conversion rate optimisation (CRO) for Zen Maitri, where not only did the conversion rate increase, but customer engagement and page scrolling percentages improved as well.[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][/vc_column][vc_column width=”3/12″][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row row_height_percent=”0″ override_padding=”yes” h_padding=”5″ top_padding=”2″ bottom_padding=”2″ overlay_alpha=”50″ gutter_size=”3″ column_width_percent=”100″ shift_y=”0″ z_index=”0″ content_parallax=”0″ uncode_shortcode_id=”209535″][vc_column width=”1/1″][vc_separator sep_color=”color-gyho” uncode_shortcode_id=”612153″ sep_color_type=”uncode-palette”][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row row_height_percent=”0″ override_padding=”yes” h_padding=”2″ top_padding=”3″ bottom_padding=”2″ overlay_alpha=”50″ gutter_size=”3″ column_width_percent=”100″ shift_y=”0″ z_index=”0″ content_parallax=”0″ uncode_shortcode_id=”277652″][vc_column width=”3/12″][/vc_column][vc_column column_width_percent=”100″ gutter_size=”4″ overlay_alpha=”50″ shift_x=”0″ shift_y=”0″ shift_y_down=”0″ z_index=”0″ medium_width=”0″ mobile_width=”0″ width=”6/12″ uncode_shortcode_id=”191092″][vc_row_inner][vc_column_inner width=”1/1″][vc_custom_heading uncode_shortcode_id=”225096″]1. Improve Your Website Speed[/vc_custom_heading][vc_column_text uncode_shortcode_id=”313221″]Slow-loading websites drive visitors away. For Shopify stores, it’s important to load within 3 seconds to achieve the best results.[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][vc_row_inner][vc_column_inner width=”1/1″][vc_custom_heading heading_semantic=”h3″ text_size=”h3″ uncode_shortcode_id=”250129″]Why Speed Matters[/vc_custom_heading][vc_column_text uncode_shortcode_id=”468882″]- 53% of users abandon websites that take longer than 3 seconds to load.

– Faster websites rank better on Google, which improves organic traffic.[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][vc_row_inner][vc_column_inner width=”1/1″][vc_custom_heading heading_semantic=”h3″ text_size=”h3″ uncode_shortcode_id=”175153″]Quick Fixes[/vc_custom_heading][vc_column_text uncode_shortcode_id=”108678″]- Use Shopify’s free Online Store Speed Report

– Compress your images with free tools like TinyPNG or Crush.pics.

– Reduce the number of apps your site has running in the background.

– Choose a lightweight, optimised Shopify theme like Dawn.[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][vc_row_inner][vc_column_inner width=”1/1″][vc_custom_heading heading_semantic=”h3″ text_size=”h3″ uncode_shortcode_id=”158631″]Example[/vc_custom_heading][vc_column_text uncode_shortcode_id=”208462″]

When I redesign websites, I always use Dawn as a starting point. It’s lightweight, fast, and built with Shopify’s best practices in mind.

Many themes come with excessive functionality and sections that don’t suit every niche or sector. For example, a fashion-focused theme might include a “Shop the Look” section, which would be irrelevant for a grocery store.

Creating bespoke sections tailored to your business will enhance the user experience while keeping the theme lean and efficient—resulting in a faster, more optimised site.

Check out the Window Fleur Case Study which was built using Dawn as a starting point.[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][/vc_column][vc_column width=”3/12″][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row row_height_percent=”0″ override_padding=”yes” h_padding=”5″ top_padding=”2″ bottom_padding=”2″ overlay_alpha=”50″ gutter_size=”3″ column_width_percent=”100″ shift_y=”0″ z_index=”0″ content_parallax=”0″ uncode_shortcode_id=”209535″][vc_column width=”1/1″][vc_separator sep_color=”color-gyho” uncode_shortcode_id=”612153″ sep_color_type=”uncode-palette”][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row row_height_percent=”0″ override_padding=”yes” h_padding=”2″ top_padding=”3″ bottom_padding=”2″ overlay_alpha=”50″ gutter_size=”3″ column_width_percent=”100″ shift_y=”0″ z_index=”0″ content_parallax=”0″ uncode_shortcode_id=”277652″][vc_column width=”3/12″][/vc_column][vc_column column_width_percent=”100″ gutter_size=”4″ overlay_alpha=”50″ shift_x=”0″ shift_y=”0″ shift_y_down=”0″ z_index=”0″ medium_width=”0″ mobile_width=”0″ width=”6/12″ uncode_shortcode_id=”191092″][vc_row_inner][vc_column_inner width=”1/1″][vc_custom_heading uncode_shortcode_id=”310631″]2. Optimise Product Pages[/vc_custom_heading][vc_column_text uncode_shortcode_id=”145796″]

Your product pages should be clear, engaging, and persuasive to convert visitors into buyers.

[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][vc_row_inner][vc_column_inner width=”1/1″][vc_custom_heading heading_semantic=”h3″ text_size=”h3″ uncode_shortcode_id=”184604″]Key Enhancements[/vc_custom_heading][vc_column_text uncode_shortcode_id=”210607″]- High-quality product images and videos. Use multiple angles and lifestyle shots.

– Detailed, benefit-driven product descriptions. Highlight what makes your product unique.

– Clear pricing, shipping, and return information. No hidden costs!

– Customer reviews and testimonials. Social proof boosts trust and conversions.

One often-overlooked element on product pages is helping customers compare options. Here’s how product comparison UX can reduce choice overload and lift conversions.

For a deep dive into creating high-converting product pages, check out Shopify’s guide to product pages.[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][vc_row_inner][vc_column_inner width=”1/1″][vc_custom_heading heading_semantic=”h3″ text_size=”h3″ uncode_shortcode_id=”158631″]Example[/vc_custom_heading][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][vc_row_inner row_inner_height_percent=”0″ overlay_alpha=”50″ gutter_size=”6″ shift_y=”0″ z_index=”0″ uncode_shortcode_id=”629001″][vc_column_inner width=”1/2″][vc_single_image media=”145891″ media_width_percent=”100″ shape=”img-round” shadow=”yes” shadow_weight=”sm” advanced=”yes” media_overlay_opacity=”50″ media_overlay_anim=”no” media_text_anim=”no” media_image_anim=”no” media_padding=”2″ uncode_shortcode_id=”200771″][vc_column_text uncode_shortcode_id=”100482″]Before[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width=”1/2″][vc_single_image media=”145905″ media_width_percent=”100″ shape=”img-round” shadow=”yes” shadow_weight=”sm” advanced=”yes” media_overlay_opacity=”50″ media_overlay_anim=”no” media_text_anim=”no” media_image_anim=”no” media_padding=”2″ uncode_shortcode_id=”214292″][vc_column_text uncode_shortcode_id=”190914″]After custom CRO work[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][vc_column_text uncode_shortcode_id=”126617″]The product page required some enhancements, including a design tweak for improved visual calmness, as there were too many styles and backgrounds competing for attention.

It was essential to establish a clear hierarchy instead of overwhelming the user with too much information above the fold.

I decided to place the Trustpilot rating at the very top to build trust from the outset. Following that, I included the key elements—product image, title, price, and review rating—on the initial screen, along with a sticky “Add to Cart” button.

This layout provides users with all the essential information they need before they scroll down. The rest of the page features a clear content hierarchy, utilising bullet points and call-outs to assist readers in scanning the information. Additionally, more detailed information is housed in accordions for easy access.

Take a look at the final product page for Zen Maitri Nerve Oil.[/vc_column_text][/vc_column][vc_column width=”3/12″][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row row_height_percent=”0″ override_padding=”yes” h_padding=”5″ top_padding=”2″ bottom_padding=”2″ overlay_alpha=”50″ gutter_size=”3″ column_width_percent=”100″ shift_y=”0″ z_index=”0″ content_parallax=”0″ uncode_shortcode_id=”209535″][vc_column width=”1/1″][vc_separator sep_color=”color-gyho” uncode_shortcode_id=”612153″ sep_color_type=”uncode-palette”][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row row_height_percent=”0″ override_padding=”yes” h_padding=”2″ top_padding=”3″ bottom_padding=”2″ overlay_alpha=”50″ gutter_size=”3″ column_width_percent=”100″ shift_y=”0″ z_index=”0″ content_parallax=”0″ uncode_shortcode_id=”277652″][vc_column width=”3/12″][/vc_column][vc_column column_width_percent=”100″ gutter_size=”4″ overlay_alpha=”50″ shift_x=”0″ shift_y=”0″ shift_y_down=”0″ z_index=”0″ medium_width=”0″ mobile_width=”0″ width=”6/12″ uncode_shortcode_id=”191092″][vc_row_inner][vc_column_inner width=”1/1″][vc_custom_heading uncode_shortcode_id=”668106″]3. Simplify the Checkout Process[/vc_custom_heading][vc_column_text uncode_shortcode_id=”202693″]

A complicated checkout is one of the biggest conversion killers. Reducing friction can lead to more completed purchases.

[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][vc_row_inner][vc_column_inner width=”1/1″][vc_custom_heading heading_semantic=”h3″ text_size=”h3″ uncode_shortcode_id=”615510″]How can you simplify the checkout process?[/vc_custom_heading][vc_column_text uncode_shortcode_id=”191486″]- Enable Shopify’s one-page checkout for faster purchases.

– Offer guest checkout to avoid unnecessary sign-ups.

– Display multiple payment options, including Apple Pay, Google Pay, and Klarna.

– Reduce checkout fields to the essentials.

For best practices, check out Baymard Institute’s research on checkout optimisation.[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][vc_row_inner row_inner_height_percent=”0″ overlay_alpha=”50″ gutter_size=”5″ shift_y=”0″ z_index=”0″ uncode_shortcode_id=”316664″][vc_column_inner column_width_percent=”100″ gutter_size=”5″ overlay_alpha=”50″ shift_x=”0″ shift_y=”0″ shift_y_down=”0″ z_index=”0″ medium_width=”0″ mobile_width=”0″ width=”1/1″ uncode_shortcode_id=”144169″][vc_custom_heading heading_semantic=”h3″ text_size=”h3″ uncode_shortcode_id=”158631″]Example[/vc_custom_heading][vc_single_image media=”145907″ media_width_percent=”100″ shape=”img-round” shadow=”yes” shadow_weight=”sm” uncode_shortcode_id=”175880″][vc_column_text uncode_shortcode_id=”654517″]The Zen Maitri checkout has the 1 page checkout enabled. Allowing the user to scroll through the entire checkout in one go. Even easier if you are like me and have the autofill set up on your device.

Find out more about the Shopify 1 page checkout[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][/vc_column][vc_column width=”3/12″][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row row_height_percent=”0″ override_padding=”yes” h_padding=”5″ top_padding=”2″ bottom_padding=”2″ overlay_alpha=”50″ gutter_size=”3″ column_width_percent=”100″ shift_y=”0″ z_index=”0″ content_parallax=”0″ uncode_shortcode_id=”209535″][vc_column width=”1/1″][vc_separator sep_color=”color-gyho” uncode_shortcode_id=”612153″ sep_color_type=”uncode-palette”][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row row_height_percent=”0″ override_padding=”yes” h_padding=”2″ top_padding=”3″ bottom_padding=”2″ overlay_alpha=”50″ gutter_size=”3″ column_width_percent=”100″ shift_y=”0″ z_index=”0″ content_parallax=”0″ uncode_shortcode_id=”277652″][vc_column width=”3/12″][/vc_column][vc_column column_width_percent=”100″ gutter_size=”4″ overlay_alpha=”50″ shift_x=”0″ shift_y=”0″ shift_y_down=”0″ z_index=”0″ medium_width=”0″ mobile_width=”0″ width=”6/12″ uncode_shortcode_id=”191092″][vc_row_inner][vc_column_inner width=”1/1″][vc_custom_heading uncode_shortcode_id=”197547″]4. Build Trust with Social Proof[/vc_custom_heading][vc_column_text uncode_shortcode_id=”117423″]

People trust real experiences from other buyers. 79% of consumers trust online reviews as much as personal recommendations.

[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][vc_row_inner][vc_column_inner width=”1/1″][vc_custom_heading heading_semantic=”h3″ text_size=”h3″ uncode_shortcode_id=”173021″]Ways to add trust[/vc_custom_heading][vc_column_text uncode_shortcode_id=”198750″]- Display customer reviews using apps like Judge.me or Loox.

– Showcase trust badges (secure checkout, money-back guarantee, etc.).

– Add an “As Seen In” section featuring press mentions or influencer partnerships.

– Offer a solid money-back guarantee to reduce purchase hesitation.

The small design details that reinforce trust, like cart animations, sticky add-to-cart buttons, and progress indicators, fall under the broader topic of microinteractions. Read more about how they improve the Shopify purchase journey.[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][vc_row_inner row_inner_height_percent=”0″ overlay_alpha=”50″ gutter_size=”5″ shift_y=”0″ z_index=”0″ uncode_shortcode_id=”316664″][vc_column_inner column_width_percent=”100″ gutter_size=”5″ overlay_alpha=”50″ shift_x=”0″ shift_y=”0″ shift_y_down=”0″ z_index=”0″ medium_width=”0″ mobile_width=”0″ width=”1/1″ uncode_shortcode_id=”144169″][vc_custom_heading heading_semantic=”h3″ text_size=”h3″ uncode_shortcode_id=”158631″]Example[/vc_custom_heading][vc_single_image media=”145911″ media_width_percent=”40″ shape=”img-round” shadow=”yes” shadow_weight=”sm” advanced=”yes” advanced_videos=”yes” media_overlay_opacity=”50″ media_overlay_anim=”no” media_text_anim=”no” media_padding=”2″ mobile_videos=”autoplay” uncode_shortcode_id=”154535″][vc_column_text uncode_shortcode_id=”143286″]Zen Maitri use the Loox platform which utilises video reviews.

Some key takeaways for having video reviews

– Testimonial videos on sales pages increase conversions by 80%.

– Around 72% of customers trust a brand more with positive video testimonials and reviews.

– Research shows that company websites with video content are 53 times more likely to appear on Google’s first page.

Read 15 Shocking Video Testimonial Statistics (New Data)[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][/vc_column][vc_column width=”3/12″][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row row_height_percent=”0″ override_padding=”yes” h_padding=”5″ top_padding=”2″ bottom_padding=”2″ overlay_alpha=”50″ gutter_size=”3″ column_width_percent=”100″ shift_y=”0″ z_index=”0″ content_parallax=”0″ uncode_shortcode_id=”209535″][vc_column width=”1/1″][vc_separator sep_color=”color-gyho” uncode_shortcode_id=”612153″ sep_color_type=”uncode-palette”][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row row_height_percent=”0″ override_padding=”yes” h_padding=”2″ top_padding=”3″ bottom_padding=”2″ overlay_alpha=”50″ gutter_size=”3″ column_width_percent=”100″ shift_y=”0″ z_index=”0″ content_parallax=”0″ uncode_shortcode_id=”277652″][vc_column width=”3/12″][/vc_column][vc_column column_width_percent=”100″ gutter_size=”4″ overlay_alpha=”50″ shift_x=”0″ shift_y=”0″ shift_y_down=”0″ z_index=”0″ medium_width=”0″ mobile_width=”0″ width=”6/12″ uncode_shortcode_id=”191092″][vc_row_inner][vc_column_inner width=”1/1″][vc_custom_heading uncode_shortcode_id=”623339″]5. Offer Free Shipping & Clear Return Policies[/vc_custom_heading][vc_column_text uncode_shortcode_id=”196107″]

Many customers abandon their cart when they see unexpected shipping costs. 48% of shoppers say free shipping influences their buying decisions.

[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][vc_row_inner][vc_column_inner width=”1/1″][vc_custom_heading heading_semantic=”h3″ text_size=”h3″ uncode_shortcode_id=”131557″]What You Can Do[/vc_custom_heading][vc_column_text uncode_shortcode_id=”104655″]- Offer free shipping (either sitewide or above a certain amount).

– Clearly state your return and refund policy on product pages.

– Use urgency tactics like “Limited stock” or “Only 2 left in stock.”

– Offer a simple return process—Shopify’s guide to return policies provides best practices.[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][vc_row_inner row_inner_height_percent=”0″ overlay_alpha=”50″ gutter_size=”5″ shift_y=”0″ z_index=”0″ uncode_shortcode_id=”316664″][vc_column_inner column_width_percent=”100″ gutter_size=”5″ overlay_alpha=”50″ shift_x=”0″ shift_y=”0″ shift_y_down=”0″ z_index=”0″ medium_width=”0″ mobile_width=”0″ width=”1/1″ uncode_shortcode_id=”144169″][vc_custom_heading heading_semantic=”h3″ text_size=”h3″ uncode_shortcode_id=”158631″]Example[/vc_custom_heading][vc_single_image media=”145916″ media_width_percent=”40″ shape=”img-round” shadow=”yes” shadow_weight=”sm” advanced=”yes” advanced_videos=”yes” media_overlay_opacity=”50″ media_overlay_anim=”no” media_text_anim=”no” media_padding=”2″ mobile_videos=”autoplay” uncode_shortcode_id=”720867″][vc_column_text uncode_shortcode_id=”203026″]For the Zen Maitri Store I brought in the Free shipping threshold right next to the add to cart button. Then the more in-depth shipping information is in the accordion so the user doesn’t have to go off the page to find out more.

The Rebuy App has also been utilised in the cart so there is a clear message if you have hit the free shipping threshold. The bonus with this app is that you can have different levels to hit. First level is free shipping, second level is for a free gift. This is a great way to boos the average order value.

Check out the Delli website for a great example of well placed delivery messaging and the upsells in the cart.[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][/vc_column][vc_column width=”3/12″][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row row_height_percent=”0″ override_padding=”yes” h_padding=”5″ top_padding=”2″ bottom_padding=”2″ overlay_alpha=”50″ gutter_size=”3″ column_width_percent=”100″ shift_y=”0″ z_index=”0″ content_parallax=”0″ uncode_shortcode_id=”209535″][vc_column width=”1/1″][vc_separator sep_color=”color-gyho” uncode_shortcode_id=”612153″ sep_color_type=”uncode-palette”][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row row_height_percent=”0″ override_padding=”yes” h_padding=”2″ top_padding=”3″ bottom_padding=”2″ overlay_alpha=”50″ gutter_size=”3″ column_width_percent=”100″ shift_y=”0″ z_index=”0″ content_parallax=”0″ uncode_shortcode_id=”277652″][vc_column width=”3/12″][/vc_column][vc_column column_width_percent=”100″ gutter_size=”4″ overlay_alpha=”50″ shift_x=”0″ shift_y=”0″ shift_y_down=”0″ z_index=”0″ medium_width=”0″ mobile_width=”0″ width=”6/12″ uncode_shortcode_id=”191092″][vc_row_inner][vc_column_inner width=”1/1″][vc_custom_heading uncode_shortcode_id=”149222″]6. Leverage Email & SMS Remarketing[/vc_custom_heading][vc_column_text uncode_shortcode_id=”783633″]

Not all customers buy on their first visit. Retarget them effectively to bring them back.

[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][vc_row_inner][vc_column_inner width=”1/1″][vc_custom_heading heading_semantic=”h3″ text_size=”h3″ uncode_shortcode_id=”208790″]Tactics to try[/vc_custom_heading][vc_column_text uncode_shortcode_id=”103895″]- Send abandoned cart emails using Shopify Email or Klaviyo.

– Use SMS marketing tools like Postscript to send reminders and exclusive discounts.

– Offer first-time buyer discounts through pop-ups.

– For more on abandoned cart recovery, read Shopify’s blog on abandoned carts.[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][/vc_column][vc_column width=”3/12″][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row row_height_percent=”0″ override_padding=”yes” h_padding=”5″ top_padding=”2″ bottom_padding=”2″ overlay_alpha=”50″ gutter_size=”3″ column_width_percent=”100″ shift_y=”0″ z_index=”0″ content_parallax=”0″ uncode_shortcode_id=”209535″][vc_column width=”1/1″][vc_separator sep_color=”color-gyho” uncode_shortcode_id=”612153″ sep_color_type=”uncode-palette”][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row row_height_percent=”0″ override_padding=”yes” h_padding=”2″ top_padding=”3″ bottom_padding=”5″ overlay_alpha=”50″ gutter_size=”3″ column_width_percent=”100″ shift_y=”0″ z_index=”0″ content_parallax=”0″ uncode_shortcode_id=”557712″][vc_column width=”3/12″][/vc_column][vc_column column_width_percent=”100″ gutter_size=”4″ overlay_alpha=”50″ shift_x=”0″ shift_y=”0″ shift_y_down=”0″ z_index=”0″ medium_width=”0″ mobile_width=”0″ width=”6/12″ uncode_shortcode_id=”191092″][vc_row_inner][vc_column_inner width=”1/1″][vc_custom_heading uncode_shortcode_id=”765161″]7. Personalise the Shopping Experience[/vc_custom_heading][vc_column_text uncode_shortcode_id=”121645″]

Personalisation makes customers feel valued and can increase conversion rates significantly.

[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][vc_row_inner][vc_column_inner width=”1/1″][vc_custom_heading heading_semantic=”h3″ text_size=”h3″ uncode_shortcode_id=”627980″]Ways to do this[/vc_custom_heading][vc_column_text uncode_shortcode_id=”819422″]- Use product recommendation apps like LimeSpot to show “Recommended for You” products.

– Shopbox takes AI to the next level, integrating personalisation at every touchpoint—from a dedicated Shopify section to a chatbot-style button and even fully tailored emails.

– Enable personalised discount pop-ups based on user behaviour.

– Implement a chatbot (like Tidio) to offer real-time support.[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][/vc_column][vc_column width=”3/12″][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row row_height_percent=”0″ override_padding=”yes” h_padding=”5″ top_padding=”2″ bottom_padding=”2″ overlay_alpha=”50″ gutter_size=”3″ column_width_percent=”100″ shift_y=”0″ z_index=”0″ content_parallax=”0″ uncode_shortcode_id=”209535″][vc_column width=”1/1″][vc_separator sep_color=”color-gyho” uncode_shortcode_id=”612153″ sep_color_type=”uncode-palette”][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row row_height_percent=”0″ override_padding=”yes” h_padding=”2″ top_padding=”4″ bottom_padding=”5″ overlay_alpha=”50″ gutter_size=”3″ column_width_percent=”100″ shift_y=”0″ z_index=”0″ content_parallax=”0″ uncode_shortcode_id=”621858″][vc_column width=”3/12″][/vc_column][vc_column column_width_percent=”100″ gutter_size=”4″ overlay_alpha=”50″ shift_x=”0″ shift_y=”0″ shift_y_down=”0″ z_index=”0″ medium_width=”0″ mobile_width=”0″ width=”6/12″ uncode_shortcode_id=”191092″][vc_row_inner][vc_column_inner width=”1/1″][vc_custom_heading uncode_shortcode_id=”715812″]Want expert help optimising your Shopify store?[/vc_custom_heading][vc_column_text uncode_shortcode_id=”167806″]

A high conversion rate isn’t just about having great products—it’s about optimising every step of the customer journey. From site speed and product pages to checkout flow, trust signals, and retargeting efforts, each element plays a role in turning visitors into loyal customers.

If you’re ready to grow your Shopify store, a UX audit is a great place to start. I begin by analysing your Google GA4 data, then walk through the entire purchasing journey with real user behaviour in mind. Using a Miro board, I annotate screenshots with insights on what’s working, what’s not, and actionable ideas to improve conversions. Read more about my process and how you could work with a Shopify conversion rate optimisation expert. For a deeper read on why conversion optimisation is still fundamentally a human discipline, read this article on why CRO can’t be automated.

Would you like a UX & Heuristic Review of your site? gutter_size=”3″ column_padding=”2″ title=”What is a good conversion rate for a Shopify store?” tab_id=”1753877405-1-5215d5-517d4844-077a2e8a-a3526311-54cd”][vc_column_text text_color=”color-nhtu” uncode_shortcode_id=”519472″ text_color_type=”uncode-palette”]

The average Shopify store converts at around 1.4%, but the top 20% of stores convert at 3.2% or above. A “good” conversion rate varies by industry — fashion and apparel often sits lower (around 1–2%) while subscription or consumable products can reach 4–5%. Rather than benchmarking against a single number, the goal is consistent improvement on your own baseline.

[/vc_column_text][/vc_accordion_tab][vc_accordion_tab gutter_size=”3″ column_padding=”2″ title=”What are the most common reasons Shopify stores have low conversion rates?” tab_id=”1753877405-2-3015d5-517d4844-077a2e8a-a3526311-54cd”][vc_column_text text_color=”color-nhtu” uncode_shortcode_id=”199479″ text_color_type=”uncode-palette”]The most frequent culprits are slow page speed (especially on mobile), unclear product pages that don’t answer buyer objections, a complicated or untrustworthy checkout experience, and weak or absent social proof. In most stores I audit, the biggest issue isn’t any single thing — it’s several small friction points adding up throughout the customer journey.[/vc_column_text][/vc_accordion_tab][vc_accordion_tab gutter_size=”3″ column_padding=”2″ title=”How much can CRO realistically improve my revenue?” tab_id=”1753883631279-2-815d5-517d4844-077a2e8a-a3526311-54cd”][vc_column_text text_color=”color-nhtu” uncode_shortcode_id=”812169″ text_color_type=”uncode-palette”]Even a 0.5% improvement in conversion rate can make a significant difference to revenue. If your store does £50,000 a month in revenue at a 1.5% conversion rate, getting to 2% would increase revenue by roughly £16,700 a month without changing your traffic at all. This is why CRO often has a better ROI than increasing ad spend.[/vc_column_text][/vc_accordion_tab][vc_accordion_tab gutter_size=”3″ column_padding=”2″ title=”Does site speed really affect conversion rates?” tab_id=”1753883631279-2-815d5-517d4844-077a2e8a-a35226311-54cd”][vc_column_text text_color=”color-nhtu” uncode_shortcode_id=”120053″ text_color_type=”uncode-palette”]Yes, significantly. Research consistently shows that a one-second delay in page load time can reduce conversions by up to 20%. On mobile, where the majority of Shopify traffic now comes from, this effect is even more pronounced. Slow themes, unoptimised images, and too many installed apps are the most common causes on Shopify stores.[/vc_column_text][/vc_accordion_tab][vc_accordion_tab gutter_size=”3″ column_padding=”2″ title=”Should I run A/B tests on my Shopify store?” tab_id=”1753883631279-2-815d5-517d4844-077a2e8a-a352276311-54cd”][vc_column_text text_color=”color-nhtu” uncode_shortcode_id=”190033″ text_color_type=”uncode-palette”]A/B testing is valuable, but only once you have enough traffic to generate statistically significant results — typically at least a few thousand sessions per month per test. For smaller stores, making informed design and copy improvements based on user behaviour data (heatmaps, session recordings) is usually more effective than trying to run formal tests with insufficient traffic.[/vc_column_text][/vc_accordion_tab][vc_accordion_tab gutter_size=”3″ column_padding=”2″ title=”What’s the difference between UX design and CRO?” tab_id=”1753883631279-2-815d5-517d4844-077a2e8a-a3522766311-54cd”][vc_column_text text_color=”color-nhtu” uncode_shortcode_id=”232841″ text_color_type=”uncode-palette”]UX (user experience) design focuses on making your store intuitive and enjoyable to use. CRO (conversion rate optimisation) focuses specifically on removing barriers to purchase. In practice, they overlap significantly — good UX tends to improve conversion, and CRO work often identifies UX problems. The distinction matters more in theory than in practice for most Shopify stores.[/vc_column_text][/vc_accordion_tab][vc_accordion_tab gutter_size=”3″ column_padding=”2″ title=”How long does it take to see results from CRO work?” tab_id=”1753883631279-2-815d5-517d4844-077a2e8a-a35227666311-54cd”][vc_column_text text_color=”color-nhtu” uncode_shortcode_id=”181108″ text_color_type=”uncode-palette”]Quick wins — like improving product page copy, adding trust signals, or fixing mobile layout issues — can show measurable results within 2–4 weeks. Structural changes like redesigning the checkout flow or rebuilding navigation take longer to implement and test. Most stores see meaningful improvement within 60–90 days of a focused CRO engagement.[/vc_column_text][/vc_accordion_tab][/vc_accordion][/vc_column][vc_column width=”3/12″][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row mainEntity.name: What is a good conversion rate for a Shopify store?

acceptedAnswer.text: The average Shopify store converts at around 1.4%, but the top 20% of stores convert at 3.3% or above. A good conversion rate varies by industry — fashion and apparel often sits lower (around 1–2%) while subscription or consumable products can reach 4–5%. Rather than benchmarking against a single number, the goal is consistent improvement on your own baseline.

mainEntity.name: What are the most common reasons Shopify stores have low conversion rates?

acceptedAnswer.text: The most frequent culprits are slow page speed (especially on mobile), unclear product pages that do not answer buyer objections, a complicated or untrustworthy checkout experience, and weak or absent social proof. In most store audits, the biggest issue is not any single thing — it is several small friction points adding up throughout the customer journey.

mainEntity.name: How much can CRO realistically improve my revenue?

acceptedAnswer.text: Even a 0.5% improvement in conversion rate can make a significant difference to revenue. If your store does £50,000 a month in revenue at a 1.5% conversion rate, getting to 2% would increase revenue by roughly £16,700 a month without changing your traffic at all. This is why CRO often has a better ROI than increasing ad spend.

mainEntity.name: Does site speed really affect conversion rates?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, significantly. Research consistently shows that a one-second delay in page load time can reduce conversions by up to 20%. On mobile, where the majority of Shopify traffic now comes from, this effect is even more pronounced. Slow themes, unoptimised images, and too many installed apps are the most common causes on Shopify stores.

mainEntity.name: Should I run A/B tests on my Shopify store?

acceptedAnswer.text: A/B testing is valuable, but only once you have enough traffic to generate statistically significant results — typically at least a few thousand sessions per month per test. For smaller stores, making informed design and copy improvements based on user behaviour data (heatmaps, session recordings) is usually more effective than trying to run formal tests with insufficient traffic.

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between UX design and CRO?

acceptedAnswer.text: UX (user experience) design focuses on making your store intuitive and enjoyable to use. CRO (conversion rate optimisation) focuses specifically on removing barriers to purchase. In practice, they overlap significantly — good UX tends to improve conversion, and CRO work often identifies UX problems. The distinction matters more in theory than in practice for most Shopify stores.

mainEntity.name: How long does it take to see results from CRO work?

acceptedAnswer.text: Quick wins — like improving product page copy, adding trust signals, or fixing mobile layout issues — can show measurable results within 2–4 weeks. Structural changes like redesigning the checkout flow or rebuilding navigation take longer to implement and test. Most stores see meaningful improvement within 60–90 days of a focused CRO engagement.

[vc_row row_height_percent=”0″ override_padding=”yes” h_padding=”2″ top_padding=”3″ bottom_padding=”2″ overlay_alpha=”50″ gutter_size=”3″ column_width_percent=”100″ shift_y=”0″ z_index=”0″ content_parallax=”0″ uncode_shortcode_id=”113408″][vc_column width=”3/12″][/vc_column][vc_column column_width_percent=”100″ gutter_size=”4″ overlay_alpha=”50″ shift_x=”0″ shift_y=”0″ shift_y_down=”0″ z_index=”0″ medium_width=”0″ mobile_width=”0″ width=”6/12″ uncode_shortcode_id=”191092″][vc_row_inner][vc_column_inner width=”1/1″][vc_custom_heading uncode_shortcode_id=”763538″]Introduction[/vc_custom_heading][vc_column_text uncode_shortcode_id=”125423″]

In this post, we will examine the key differences between Shopify and Shopify Plus, helping you determine which option best aligns with your eCommerce goals.

As a Shopify Expert who works with brands across both plans, I’ll walk through the key differences to help you decide.

Already know you need Plus and just want to weigh up the upgrade decision? See my Benefits of Shopify Plus: Should You Upgrade in 2026? guide, which covers the real cost-benefit maths.

[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][/vc_column][vc_column width=”3/12″][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row row_height_percent=”0″ override_padding=”yes” h_padding=”2″ top_padding=”3″ bottom_padding=”2″ overlay_alpha=”50″ gutter_size=”3″ column_width_percent=”100″ shift_y=”0″ z_index=”0″ content_parallax=”0″ uncode_shortcode_id=”113408″][vc_column width=”3/12″][/vc_column][vc_column column_width_percent=”100″ gutter_size=”4″ overlay_alpha=”50″ shift_x=”0″ shift_y=”0″ shift_y_down=”0″ z_index=”0″ medium_width=”0″ mobile_width=”0″ width=”6/12″ uncode_shortcode_id=”191092″][vc_row_inner][vc_column_inner width=”1/1″][vc_custom_heading uncode_shortcode_id=”358989″]Pricing Comparison[/vc_custom_heading][vc_column_text uncode_shortcode_id=”523453″]

Let’s start with one of the biggest deciding factors: cost.

Shopify Pricing

Plans range from £25/month (Basic) to £344/month (Advanced). These plans offer all the essential features to run a small to medium-sized online store. View Shopify pricing

Shopify Plus Pricing

Starts at around £1,600/month, with pricing scaling based on your business revenue. While this is a significant jump, it includes enterprise-level features and dedicated support tailored for fast-growing brands.Many of the world’s biggest brands run on Shopify Plus. Here’s a look at 25 of them and what makes Shopify their platform of choice. Learn more about Shopify Plus[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][/vc_column][vc_column width=”3/12″][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row row_height_percent=”0″ override_padding=”yes” h_padding=”5″ top_padding=”2″ bottom_padding=”2″ overlay_alpha=”50″ gutter_size=”3″ column_width_percent=”100″ shift_y=”0″ z_index=”0″ content_parallax=”0″ uncode_shortcode_id=”209535″][vc_column width=”1/1″][vc_separator sep_color=”color-gyho” uncode_shortcode_id=”612153″ sep_color_type=”uncode-palette”][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row row_height_percent=”0″ override_padding=”yes” h_padding=”2″ top_padding=”2″ bottom_padding=”2″ overlay_alpha=”50″ gutter_size=”3″ column_width_percent=”100″ shift_y=”0″ z_index=”0″ content_parallax=”0″ uncode_shortcode_id=”139467″][vc_column width=”3/12″][/vc_column][vc_column column_width_percent=”100″ gutter_size=”4″ overlay_alpha=”50″ shift_x=”0″ shift_y=”0″ shift_y_down=”0″ z_index=”0″ medium_width=”0″ mobile_width=”0″ width=”6/12″ uncode_shortcode_id=”191092″][vc_row_inner][vc_column_inner width=”1/1″][vc_custom_heading uncode_shortcode_id=”256307″]Features & Capabilities[/vc_custom_heading][vc_column_text uncode_shortcode_id=”990298″]

The price difference comes with a substantial boost in features. Let’s explore what you get with each option.

[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][vc_row_inner][vc_column_inner width=”1/1″][vc_custom_heading heading_semantic=”h3″ text_size=”h3″ uncode_shortcode_id=”121071″]Customisation & Design[/vc_custom_heading][vc_column_text uncode_shortcode_id=”160832″]

Let’s start with one of the biggest deciding factors: cost.

Shopify

Access to themes and the ability to customise with the theme editor or by editing Liquid files.

Shopify Plus

Full control over your site, including a completely customisable checkout, perfect for optimising conversions.This is where working with a Shopify designer on a bespoke store build really pays off; you get full control of the design rather than being constrained by theme settings. Shopify Plus checkout customisation

[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][vc_row_inner][vc_column_inner width=”1/1″][vc_custom_heading heading_semantic=”h3″ text_size=”h3″ uncode_shortcode_id=”259623″]Checkout Experience[/vc_custom_heading][vc_column_text uncode_shortcode_id=”190697″]

Shopify

Standard checkout with limited customisation.

Shopify Plus

Tailor your checkout experience with custom fields, branded elements, and dynamic discounting.

[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][vc_row_inner][vc_column_inner width=”1/1″][vc_custom_heading heading_semantic=”h3″ text_size=”h3″ uncode_shortcode_id=”186827″]Automation & Workflows[/vc_custom_heading][vc_column_text uncode_shortcode_id=”235956″]

Shopify

Basic automation features.

Shopify Plus

Shopify Flow lets you create advanced workflows, like automating inventory alerts or segmenting VIP customers. Discover Shopify Flow

[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][vc_row_inner][vc_column_inner width=”1/1″][vc_custom_heading heading_semantic=”h3″ text_size=”h3″ uncode_shortcode_id=”132794″]API Access & Integrations[/vc_custom_heading][vc_column_text uncode_shortcode_id=”137163″]

Shopify

Access to standard APIs.

Shopify Plus

Greater API rate limits and access to more advanced APIs for custom app development. Shopify API documentation

[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][vc_row_inner][vc_column_inner width=”1/1″][vc_custom_heading heading_semantic=”h3″ text_size=”h3″ uncode_shortcode_id=”838380″]Support & Guidance[/vc_custom_heading][vc_column_text uncode_shortcode_id=”609752″]

Shopify

24/7 support via live chat, email, and phone.

Shopify Plus

A dedicated Merchant Success Manager, plus priority support and strategic guidance. Shopify support

[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][/vc_column][vc_column width=”3/12″][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row row_height_percent=”0″ override_padding=”yes” h_padding=”5″ top_padding=”2″ bottom_padding=”2″ overlay_alpha=”50″ gutter_size=”3″ column_width_percent=”100″ shift_y=”0″ z_index=”0″ content_parallax=”0″ uncode_shortcode_id=”209535″][vc_column width=”1/1″][vc_separator sep_color=”color-gyho” uncode_shortcode_id=”612153″ sep_color_type=”uncode-palette”][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row][vc_column width=”3/12″][/vc_column][vc_column width=”6/12″][vc_custom_heading uncode_shortcode_id=”206644″]Which Shopify plan Should I Use?[/vc_custom_heading][vc_column_text uncode_shortcode_id=”838244″]

Choosing between Shopify and Shopify Plus ultimately depends on your business’s size, growth stage, and specific needs.

Shopify

Ideal for small to medium-sized businesses that need a robust, easy-to-use platform without a hefty price tag.

Shopify Plus

Best for large or rapidly growing brands (typically generating £750k+ per year) that need advanced features, scalability, and hands-on support.[/vc_column_text][/vc_column][vc_column width=”3/12″][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row row_height_percent=”0″ override_padding=”yes” h_padding=”5″ top_padding=”2″ bottom_padding=”2″ overlay_alpha=”50″ gutter_size=”3″ column_width_percent=”100″ shift_y=”0″ z_index=”0″ content_parallax=”0″ uncode_shortcode_id=”209535″][vc_column width=”1/1″][vc_separator sep_color=”color-gyho” uncode_shortcode_id=”612153″ sep_color_type=”uncode-palette”][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row][vc_column width=”3/12″][/vc_column][vc_column width=”6/12″][vc_custom_heading uncode_shortcode_id=”136073″]Final Thoughts[/vc_custom_heading][vc_column_text uncode_shortcode_id=”116218″]

If you’re a smaller business or just starting out, Shopify’s core plans likely offer everything you need to build and run a successful online store. But if you’re scaling quickly, need a custom checkout, or want enterprise-level automation, Shopify Plus could be the game-changer that helps you level up.

If you’re ready to build or upgrade your Shopify store, I’d love to help. Take a look at my Shopify web design services and get in touch.

Feel free to contact me — I’d love to help you navigate your Shopify journey and build a store that grows with your business![/vc_column_text][/vc_column][vc_column gutter_size=”3″ column_padding=”2″ title=”What is the main difference between Shopify and Shopify Plus?” tab_id=”1753877405-1-5215d5-517d4844-077a2e8a-a352695f-51bb”][vc_column_text text_color=”color-nhtu” uncode_shortcode_id=”182877″ text_color_type=”uncode-palette”]

The main differences come down to customisation, scale, and support. Shopify Plus gives you full control over the checkout experience (something standard Shopify locks down), access to higher API rate limits for complex integrations, Shopify Flow for advanced automation, and a dedicated merchant success manager. It’s designed for brands that have outgrown the standard plan’s limitations.

[/vc_column_text][/vc_accordion_tab][vc_accordion_tab gutter_size=”3″ column_padding=”2″ title=”How much does Shopify Plus cost?” tab_id=”1753877405-2-3015d5-517d4844-077a2e8a-a352695f-51bb”][vc_column_text text_color=”color-nhtu” uncode_shortcode_id=”381562″ text_color_type=”uncode-palette”]Shopify Plus pricing typically starts from around £1,800 per month on a long-term contract, or approximately £1,950 per month on a shorter rolling agreement.

For high-revenue stores generating more than £630,000 per month, pricing can shift to a revenue-based model (around 0.35% of monthly turnover), allowing costs to scale alongside growth. This structure makes Shopify Plus most cost-effective for brands operating at significant ecommerce volume.[/vc_column_text][/vc_accordion_tab][vc_accordion_tab gutter_size=”3″ column_padding=”2″ title=”When should a brand upgrade from Shopify to Shopify Plus?” tab_id=”1753883631279-2-815d5-517d4844-077a2e8a-a352695f-51bb”][vc_column_text text_color=”color-nhtu” uncode_shortcode_id=”230718″ text_color_type=”uncode-palette”]The clearest triggers are: when you need to customise the checkout beyond what standard Shopify allows; when your store requires complex B2B or wholesale functionality; when you’re processing over £1 million per year and the transaction fees on standard Shopify start to add up significantly; or when your integrations are hitting API rate limits. For most stores, these issues don’t arise until they’re well past the £500k–£1m annual revenue mark.[/vc_column_text][/vc_accordion_tab][vc_accordion_tab gutter_size=”3″ column_padding=”2″ title=”Can you customise checkout on standard Shopify?” tab_id=”1753883631279-2-815d5-517d4844-077a2e8a-a3522695f-51bb”][vc_column_text text_color=”color-nhtu” uncode_shortcode_id=”148015″ text_color_type=”uncode-palette”]Standard Shopify allows limited checkout customisation — you can change colours and add a logo, but you cannot modify the checkout layout, add custom fields, or embed third-party scripts. Shopify Plus unlocks full checkout customisation through checkout.liquid (and increasingly through Checkout Extensibility), which is why it’s so valuable for brands with specific upsell flows or B2B requirements.[/vc_column_text][/vc_accordion_tab][vc_accordion_tab gutter_size=”3″ column_padding=”2″ title=”Is Shopify Plus worth the cost?” tab_id=”1753883631279-2-815d5-517d4844-077a2e8a-a35227695f-51bb”][vc_column_text text_color=”color-nhtu” uncode_shortcode_id=”114533″ text_color_type=”uncode-palette”]For the right business, yes — the combination of reduced transaction fees (Shopify Plus waives third-party transaction fees entirely), checkout customisation, and automation capabilities can deliver significant ROI. However, for stores doing under £500k annually, the cost of Plus rarely justifies itself. Often referred to as the “premium” version, what exactly distinguishes it from the standard Shopify? More importantly, is it a worthwhile investment for your business?

mainEntity.name: What is the main difference between Shopify and Shopify Plus?

acceptedAnswer.text: The main differences come down to customisation, scale, and support. Shopify Plus gives you full control over the checkout experience (something standard Shopify locks down), access to higher API rate limits for complex integrations, Shopify Flow for advanced automation, and a dedicated merchant success manager. It is designed for brands that have outgrown the standard plan's limitations.

mainEntity.name: How much does Shopify Plus cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: Shopify Plus pricing starts at $2,300 per month on a three-year term, or $2,500 per month on a monthly rolling contract. For higher-revenue stores (above $800,000 per month in sales), pricing shifts to a revenue-based model at 0.25% of monthly revenue. This makes it most cost-effective for stores doing significant volume.

mainEntity.name: When should a brand upgrade from Shopify to Shopify Plus?

acceptedAnswer.text: The clearest triggers are: when you need to customise the checkout beyond what standard Shopify allows; when your store requires complex B2B or wholesale functionality; when you are processing over £1 million per year and the transaction fees on standard Shopify start to add up significantly; or when your integrations are hitting API rate limits. For most stores, these issues do not arise until they are well past the £500k–£1m annual revenue mark.

mainEntity.name: Can you customise checkout on standard Shopify?

acceptedAnswer.text: Standard Shopify allows limited checkout customisation — you can change colours and add a logo, but you cannot modify the checkout layout, add custom fields, or embed third-party scripts. Shopify Plus unlocks full checkout customisation through Checkout Extensibility, which is why it is so valuable for brands with specific upsell flows or B2B requirements.

mainEntity.name: Is Shopify Plus worth the cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: For the right business, yes — the combination of reduced transaction fees (Shopify Plus waives third-party transaction fees entirely), checkout customisation, and automation capabilities can deliver significant ROI. However, for stores doing under £500k annually, the cost of Plus rarely justifies itself. The honest answer is: it depends on which specific limitations you are hitting on your current plan.

mainEntity.name: Does Shopify Plus include dedicated support?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Shopify Plus merchants get a dedicated merchant success manager as well as priority support, including faster response times and access to Shopify's Plus-specific partner ecosystem. For growing brands, having a direct line to Shopify support rather than dealing with generic customer service is one of the practical benefits often overlooked.

title.rendered: Microinteractions in Shopify Website Design

content.rendered:
[vc_row row_height_percent=”0″ override_padding=”yes” h_padding=”2″ top_padding=”3″ bottom_padding=”2″ overlay_alpha=”50″ gutter_size=”3″ column_width_percent=”100″ shift_y=”0″ z_index=”0″ content_parallax=”0″ uncode_shortcode_id=”139026″][vc_column width=”3/12″][/vc_column][vc_column width=”6/12″][vc_custom_heading uncode_shortcode_id=”134538″]Introduction[/vc_custom_heading][vc_column_text uncode_shortcode_id=”170695″]One such detail is microinteractions, subtle yet powerful design elements that enhance usability, provide feedback, and delight users. As a Shopify Expert and UX designer, microinteractions are one of the details I focus on in every store build — because they’re often the difference between a store that feels polished and one that feels generic. Whether you’re on a social media platform, a brochure website, or a Shopify site, microinteractions can increase engagement and drive conversions by making the user journey smoother and more intuitive.[/vc_column_text][/vc_column][vc_column width=”3/12″][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row row_height_percent=”0″ override_padding=”yes” h_padding=”5″ top_padding=”2″ bottom_padding=”2″ overlay_alpha=”50″ gutter_size=”3″ column_width_percent=”100″ shift_y=”0″ z_index=”0″ content_parallax=”0″ uncode_shortcode_id=”209535″][vc_column width=”1/1″][vc_separator sep_color=”color-gyho” uncode_shortcode_id=”612153″ sep_color_type=”uncode-palette”][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row row_height_percent=”0″ override_padding=”yes” h_padding=”2″ top_padding=”3″ bottom_padding=”2″ overlay_alpha=”50″ gutter_size=”3″ column_width_percent=”100″ shift_y=”0″ z_index=”0″ content_parallax=”0″ uncode_shortcode_id=”139026″][vc_column width=”3/12″][/vc_column][vc_column width=”6/12″][vc_custom_heading uncode_shortcode_id=”104229″]What Are Microinteractions?[/vc_custom_heading][vc_column_text uncode_shortcode_id=”629619″]Microinteractions are small, functional animations or responses that help users understand system feedback, navigate easily, and feel connected to a digital product.

Some examples of microinteractions include:

✔️ The cart icon updating after an item is added in an online store.
✔️ An animation for the like button on social media.
✔️ A progress bar displayed during checkout.
✔️ A pull-to-refresh gesture in mobile apps.
✔️ A typing indicator in a messaging app.

Although these elements may seem minor, they play a significant role in enhancing overall user experience (UX). As Dan Saffer, the author of “Microinteractions: Designing with Details,” explains, “great design is in the details.”[/vc_column_text][/vc_column][vc_column width=”3/12″][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row row_height_percent=”0″ override_padding=”yes” h_padding=”5″ top_padding=”2″ bottom_padding=”2″ overlay_alpha=”50″ gutter_size=”3″ column_width_percent=”100″ shift_y=”0″ z_index=”0″ content_parallax=”0″ uncode_shortcode_id=”209535″][vc_column width=”1/1″][vc_separator sep_color=”color-gyho” uncode_shortcode_id=”612153″ sep_color_type=”uncode-palette”][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row][vc_column width=”3/12″][/vc_column][vc_column width=”6/12″][vc_custom_heading uncode_shortcode_id=”318520″]Why Microinteractions Matter[/vc_custom_heading][vc_custom_heading heading_semantic=”h3″ text_size=”h3″ uncode_shortcode_id=”300639″]1. Enhancing User Feedback[/vc_custom_heading][vc_column_text uncode_shortcode_id=”728954″]

Microinteractions offer immediate feedback for user actions. For instance, when a user clicks “Add to Cart” on an eCommerce site, they may feel uncertain about whether the action was successful. A small animation, such as a cart icon bouncing, provides instant reassurance. This kind of feedback design is central to conversion rate optimisation, it reduces uncertainty and keeps users moving through the journey.

[/vc_column_text][uncode_lottie json=”https://lottie.host/af3cea9f-f0c3-4b92-b28f-7efe7da71328/ehZGH3sAXJ.json” speed=”10″ frame_from=”0″ frame_to=”100″ media_width_percent=”30″ uncode_shortcode_id=”795522″ title=”Add to cart microinteraction”][vc_column_text uncode_shortcode_id=”144547″]Example: A small positive animation on a product card lets the user know that the product has been added to the cart.[/vc_column_text][vc_custom_heading heading_semantic=”h3″ text_size=”h3″ uncode_shortcode_id=”127445″]2. Reducing Friction & Improving Navigation[/vc_custom_heading][vc_column_text uncode_shortcode_id=”160220″]

Microinteractions help users navigate complex interfaces without feeling overwhelmed. Features like hover effects, tooltips, and animations can guide attention and enhance usability.

[/vc_column_text][uncode_lottie json=”https://lottie.host/8dd200d5-ea6b-487c-bfeb-ca57cd74f8d4/I08EIzY63O.json” speed=”10″ frame_from=”0″ frame_to=”100″ media_width_percent=”40″ uncode_shortcode_id=”106614″ title=”mobile menu microinteraction”][vc_column_text uncode_shortcode_id=”930375″]Example: The icon animation teamed up with a background overlay lets the user know that they have opened a modal.[/vc_column_text][vc_custom_heading heading_semantic=”h3″ text_size=”h3″ uncode_shortcode_id=”173997″]3. Increasing Engagement & Delight[/vc_custom_heading][vc_column_text uncode_shortcode_id=”965073″]

Small design elements enhance interfaces, making them more enjoyable and human. Animated loading indicators, playful success messages, and confetti effects can transform routine tasks into delightful moments.

[/vc_column_text][vc_single_image media=”145679″ media_width_percent=”50″ shape=”img-round” shadow=”yes” shadow_weight=”sm” advanced=”yes” advanced_videos=”yes” media_overlay_opacity=”50″ media_overlay_anim=”no” media_text_anim=”no” media_image_anim=”no” media_padding=”2″ mobile_videos=”autoplay” uncode_shortcode_id=”203067″][vc_column_text uncode_shortcode_id=”298563″]Example: The new Whistlefish Shopify website design utilised Lottie files to bring in special gamification elements to let users know they completed a stage in the purchase journey or that they have just unlocked a promotion.[/vc_column_text][/vc_column][vc_column width=”3/12″][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row row_height_percent=”0″ override_padding=”yes” h_padding=”5″ top_padding=”2″ bottom_padding=”2″ overlay_alpha=”50″ gutter_size=”3″ column_width_percent=”100″ shift_y=”0″ z_index=”0″ content_parallax=”0″ uncode_shortcode_id=”209535″][vc_column width=”1/1″][vc_separator sep_color=”color-gyho” uncode_shortcode_id=”612153″ sep_color_type=”uncode-palette”][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row][vc_column width=”3/12″][/vc_column][vc_column width=”6/12″][vc_custom_heading uncode_shortcode_id=”675224″]Microinteractions in Social Media: The Facebook Example[/vc_custom_heading][vc_column_text uncode_shortcode_id=”176228″]

Social media platforms, especially Facebook, have mastered microinteractions to keep users engaged. Some of the most effective ones include:

🎭 Reactions on posts – The evolution of the simple “Like” button into multiple reaction emojis (Love, Haha, Wow, Angry, etc.) adds emotional depth to user interactions.

💬 Typing indicators in Messenger – This subtle animation lets users know the other person is responding, making conversations feel more natural.

📢 Live video engagement – When users react to a Facebook Live video, reactions float across the screen in real time, fostering a sense of community.

🔔 Subtle notifications – Red notification badges and gentle animations draw attention to new messages or alerts without being intrusive.

These elements keep users engaged, informed, and emotionally connected to the platform—proving that microinteractions are essential to digital engagement. In fact, this article on UX Scotland explores how microinteractions can evolve into signature moments that define an entire user experience.

[/vc_column_text][vc_single_image media=”145649″ media_width_percent=”90″ shape=”img-round” shadow=”yes” shadow_weight=”sm” advanced=”yes” advanced_videos=”yes” media_overlay_opacity=”50″ media_overlay_anim=”no” media_text_anim=”no” media_image_anim=”no” media_padding=”2″ mobile_videos=”autoplay” uncode_shortcode_id=”170440″][vc_column_text uncode_shortcode_id=”140032″]Small microinteractions when users react to a post not only indicate that a button has been pressed, but also animate the emoticon, creating deeper engagement.[/vc_column_text][/vc_column][vc_column width=”3/12″][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row row_height_percent=”0″ override_padding=”yes” h_padding=”5″ top_padding=”2″ bottom_padding=”2″ overlay_alpha=”50″ gutter_size=”3″ column_width_percent=”100″ shift_y=”0″ z_index=”0″ content_parallax=”0″ uncode_shortcode_id=”209535″][vc_column width=”1/1″][vc_separator sep_color=”color-gyho” uncode_shortcode_id=”612153″ sep_color_type=”uncode-palette”][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row][vc_column width=”3/12″][/vc_column][vc_column width=”6/12″][vc_custom_heading uncode_shortcode_id=”864318″]How Microinteractions Improve the Purchase Journey on Shopify[/vc_custom_heading][vc_custom_heading heading_semantic=”h3″ text_size=”h3″ uncode_shortcode_id=”113870″]1. Product Discovery & Engagement[/vc_custom_heading][vc_column_text uncode_shortcode_id=”163314″]

In an online store, first impressions matter. Microinteractions like:

🔍 Hover animations that reveal product details.

🖼️ Zoom-in effects on product images.

⭐ Smooth rating animations that highlight reviews.

🎥 GIFs or short animations showing product usage.

🔄 360-degree product viewers that let customers rotate and explore items.

These small touches boost confidence and encourage product exploration.

[/vc_column_text][vc_custom_heading heading_semantic=”h3″ text_size=”h3″ uncode_shortcode_id=”530182″]2. Making the “Add to Cart” Process Seamless[/vc_custom_heading][vc_column_text uncode_shortcode_id=”182226″]

A satisfying visual confirmation reassures customers that their selection has been added. Effective microinteractions include:

🛒 Cart icon animations (bounce, slide-in, or number increment).

🔔 Subtle success pop-ups with “Added to Cart” messages.

⏩ Quick-buy buttons that skip unnecessary steps and speed up shopping.

📍 Sticky “Add to Cart” buttons that stay visible as customers scroll.

[/vc_column_text][vc_custom_heading heading_semantic=”h3″ text_size=”h3″ uncode_shortcode_id=”185004″]3. Enhancing the Checkout Experience[/vc_custom_heading][vc_column_text uncode_shortcode_id=”598394″]

A complicated checkout process is a conversion killer. Microinteractions help by:

✅ Step-by-step progress indicators reducing uncertainty.

🔄 Loading animations showing when payments are processing.

✏️ Editable cart previews allowing last-minute changes before checkout.

🎉 Fun order confirmation animations (confetti, checkmarks, or animated “Thank You” messages).

📦 Live order tracking microinteractions, updating shipping status in real time.

[/vc_column_text][vc_custom_heading heading_semantic=”h3″ text_size=”h3″ uncode_shortcode_id=”225542″]4. Boosting Customer Engagement Post-Purchase[/vc_custom_heading][vc_column_text uncode_shortcode_id=”188170″]

The experience shouldn’t stop after checkout! Keep customers engaged with:

📧 Interactive email confirmations (animated order status updates).

💬 Live chat bubbles with subtle pulsing effects, prompting users to ask questions.

🌟 Animated review request pop-ups encouraging customers to leave feedback.

🎁 Loyalty points counters with dynamic progress bars to track rewards.

[/vc_column_text][/vc_column][vc_column width=”3/12″][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row row_height_percent=”0″ override_padding=”yes” h_padding=”5″ top_padding=”2″ bottom_padding=”2″ overlay_alpha=”50″ gutter_size=”3″ column_width_percent=”100″ shift_y=”0″ z_index=”0″ content_parallax=”0″ uncode_shortcode_id=”209535″][vc_column width=”1/1″][vc_separator sep_color=”color-gyho” uncode_shortcode_id=”612153″ sep_color_type=”uncode-palette”][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row][vc_column width=”3/12″][/vc_column][vc_column width=”6/12″][vc_custom_heading uncode_shortcode_id=”185348″]Bringing Microinteractions into Your Shopify Store[/vc_custom_heading][vc_custom_heading heading_semantic=”h3″ text_size=”h3″ uncode_shortcode_id=”133934″]1. No-Code Solutions (Apps & Tools)[/vc_custom_heading][vc_column_text uncode_shortcode_id=”200662″]

If you’re on Shopify, there are some apps and services that can help, however you would be restricted in the UX around these. Here are some top-rated tools:

📌 PageFly – Drag-and-drop builder with interactive elements.

📌 Shogun – Adds animated buttons and hover effects.

📌 LOOX – Displays animated product reviews to build trust.

[/vc_column_text][vc_custom_heading heading_semantic=”h3″ text_size=”h3″ uncode_shortcode_id=”119347″]2. Ways to implement more bespoke microinteractions[/vc_custom_heading][vc_column_text uncode_shortcode_id=”510347″]

For more tailored solutions, developers can use:

💻 CSS animations for hover effects and transitions.

⚡ JavaScript libraries (GSAP, Lottie) for dynamic interactions.

🛒 Shopify Liquid code to trigger microinteractions at key touchpoints.

[/vc_column_text][/vc_column][vc_column width=”3/12″][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row row_height_percent=”0″ override_padding=”yes” h_padding=”5″ top_padding=”2″ bottom_padding=”2″ overlay_alpha=”50″ gutter_size=”3″ column_width_percent=”100″ shift_y=”0″ z_index=”0″ content_parallax=”0″ uncode_shortcode_id=”209535″][vc_column width=”1/1″][vc_separator sep_color=”color-gyho” uncode_shortcode_id=”612153″ sep_color_type=”uncode-palette”][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row][vc_column width=”3/12″][/vc_column][vc_column width=”6/12″][vc_custom_heading uncode_shortcode_id=”223401″]Round up. Small details, Big impact.[/vc_custom_heading][vc_column_text uncode_shortcode_id=”419119″]

Microinteractions may be small, but they elevate the entire user experience—from navigation to engagement to conversions. Whether they are small UX touches to make everything super clear for the user or using more bespoke gamification approaches to drive up customer engagement, conversion rate and loyalty there is no limits with what is achievable on the Shopify platform and using a Shopify website designer who knows what he is doing.

mainEntity.name: What are microinteractions in web design?

acceptedAnswer.text: Microinteractions are small, functional animations or design responses that happen in reaction to a user's action. Examples include a cart icon bouncing when a product is added, a button changing colour when hovered, a form field highlighting when selected, or a progress bar filling during checkout. They're called micro because they're brief and focused — but their cumulative effect on user experience and trust is significant.

mainEntity.name: How do microinteractions improve conversion rates?

acceptedAnswer.text: They reduce uncertainty at key moments in the customer journey. When a user clicks Add to Cart and nothing visually happens, they're unsure if it worked — which creates hesitation and sometimes abandonment. A clear animation confirming the action reassures them and keeps them moving toward checkout. Similarly, progress indicators during checkout reduce drop-off by showing users how close they are to completing their purchase.

mainEntity.name: Are microinteractions just decorative?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. While they can contribute to a premium feel, their primary purpose is functional: confirming actions, guiding navigation, and signalling system status. Purely decorative animations — ones that play without a user trigger and don't convey information — can actually hurt UX by slowing down interactions and distracting from the purchase path. Good microinteractions are purposeful, not decorative.

mainEntity.name: Do microinteractions slow down a Shopify store?

acceptedAnswer.text: Poorly implemented ones can, yes. Heavy JavaScript animations or too many simultaneously triggered effects add to page weight and can affect Core Web Vitals scores. Well-built microinteractions use CSS transitions or lightweight JavaScript and have a negligible impact on performance. The key is building them cleanly rather than relying on third-party animation libraries that weren't designed with Shopify performance in mind.

mainEntity.name: Can I add microinteractions to my existing Shopify theme?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, many can be added without a full rebuild. Cart animations, hover effects, sticky add-to-cart button behaviour, and progress bar elements can often be implemented with targeted CSS and small JavaScript additions. More complex interactions — like custom checkout feedback states or quiz-based product flows — typically require a bespoke build. What's achievable depends on your current theme's structure and how much it's been customised.

mainEntity.name: What Shopify pages benefit most from microinteractions?

acceptedAnswer.text: Product pages and checkout flows see the greatest impact. On product pages: image swaps on variant selection, add-to-cart feedback, and sticky CTA behaviour all reduce friction. In checkout: progress indicators and inline form validation (flagging errors before the user submits) are proven conversion improvements. Collection pages also benefit from smooth filter transitions and quick-view interactions that reduce the need to navigate away.

[vc_row row_height_percent=”0″ override_padding=”yes” h_padding=”2″ top_padding=”3″ bottom_padding=”2″ overlay_alpha=”50″ gutter_size=”3″ column_width_percent=”100″ shift_y=”0″ z_index=”0″ auto_height_device=”yes” changer_back_color=”yes” content_parallax=”0″ uncode_shortcode_id=”179757″ css=”.vc_custom_1739977313457{padding-top: 50px !important;}”][vc_column width=”3/12″][/vc_column][vc_column column_width_percent=”100″ gutter_size=”3″ style=”light” overlay_alpha=”50″ shift_x=”0″ shift_y=”0″ shift_y_down=”0″ z_index=”0″ medium_width=”0″ mobile_width=”0″ width=”6/12″ uncode_shortcode_id=”771324″][vc_custom_heading uncode_shortcode_id=”186472″]Top tips for your Homeware & Lifestyle Shopify website[/vc_custom_heading][vc_custom_heading heading_semantic=”h3″ text_size=”h3″ uncode_shortcode_id=”263161″]1. Perfect branding and design[/vc_custom_heading][vc_custom_heading heading_semantic=”h4″ text_size=”h4″ uncode_shortcode_id=”646839″]What to do[/vc_custom_heading][vc_column_text uncode_shortcode_id=”137134″]

  • Clean & clear aesthetics & messaging.
  • Have consistent imagery.
  • Highlight what makes your company unique to help get new customers buy-in and separate you from the competition.

[/vc_column_text][vc_custom_heading heading_semantic=”h4″ text_size=”h4″ uncode_shortcode_id=”205611″]Why it is important[/vc_custom_heading][vc_column_text uncode_shortcode_id=”758702″]A beautiful website design will gain trust amongst customers and boost their confidence in the quality of your products. Whilst also making it clearer and easier to use. After all, if you are selling products that imply design and beauty and your design isn’t up to scratch then it’s likely your customers won’t trust what the brand is selling.

First impressions are massive in eccommerce, when a potential customer is shopping around on multiple sites you need to stand out. The conversion could be done solely on price point, however trust in the brand also plays a huge part.[/vc_column_text][/vc_column][vc_column width=”3/12″][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row row_height_percent=”0″ override_padding=”yes” h_padding=”2″ top_padding=”5″ bottom_padding=”2″ overlay_alpha=”50″ gutter_size=”3″ column_width_percent=”100″ shift_y=”0″ z_index=”0″ changer_back_color=”yes” uncode_shortcode_id=”221145″][vc_column width=”3/12″][/vc_column][vc_column column_width_percent=”100″ gutter_size=”3″ style=”light” overlay_alpha=”50″ shift_x=”0″ shift_y=”0″ shift_y_down=”0″ z_index=”0″ medium_width=”0″ mobile_width=”0″ width=”6/12″ uncode_shortcode_id=”771324″][vc_custom_heading heading_semantic=”h3″ text_size=”h3″ uncode_shortcode_id=”169072″]2. Clear Navigation & User Journeys[/vc_custom_heading][vc_custom_heading heading_semantic=”h4″ text_size=”h4″ uncode_shortcode_id=”417197″]What to do[/vc_custom_heading][vc_column_text uncode_shortcode_id=”526478″]

  • Multiple routes into collection pages and product pages. Some users may want to shop by a room, some may want to shop by a specific styling that they are looking for.
  • Well thought out landing pages with clear sub pages and filtering.
  • Search with recommended products.

[/vc_column_text][vc_custom_heading heading_semantic=”h4″ text_size=”h4″ uncode_shortcode_id=”205611″]Why it is important[/vc_custom_heading][vc_column_text uncode_shortcode_id=”352837″]Not all users have the same needs. Some users will land on your site from a search engine. Some know exactly what they want and want it fast. Whereas some users may be engaged in the brand and only want to see what your latest products are.

So how do you make your website usable for researchers and impulse buyers?

It’s all down to a clear hierarchy. Separating different journey methods and making them easy to find. There has been a recent trend of bringing key collections out of the burger menu so they are clear and upfront on every page of your store. This works great as the user doesn’t have to open a menu and look around, saving time and clicks.

You can also visually separate them in the menu. This could be done by color, spacers or content. You could also have imagery or icons for some links and text links for others, this method works great when you have some collections that need sub pages in the menu, which creates a clear visual hierarchy. [/vc_column_text][vc_custom_heading heading_semantic=”h4″ text_size=”h4″ uncode_shortcode_id=”749073″]Examples[/vc_custom_heading][vc_column_text uncode_shortcode_id=”868462″]The new La radoute site brings some of their key collections and landing pages out of the burger menu. They even draw the eye and highlight the top offers by using their brand colour. This approach means there are less clicks for a user to get to a collection page and start shopping. [/vc_column_text][/vc_column][vc_column width=”3/12″][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row row_height_percent=”0″ override_padding=”yes” h_padding=”2″ top_padding=”2″ bottom_padding=”2″ overlay_alpha=”50″ gutter_size=”3″ column_width_percent=”100″ shift_y=”0″ z_index=”0″ changer_back_color=”yes” uncode_shortcode_id=”840521″][vc_column width=”3/12″][/vc_column][vc_column width=”6/12″][vc_single_image media=”2994″ media_width_percent=”100″ advanced_videos=”yes” mobile_videos=”autoplay” uncode_shortcode_id=”132850″][/vc_column][vc_column width=”3/12″][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row row_height_percent=”0″ override_padding=”yes” h_padding=”2″ top_padding=”5″ bottom_padding=”2″ overlay_alpha=”50″ gutter_size=”3″ column_width_percent=”100″ shift_y=”0″ z_index=”0″ changer_back_color=”yes” uncode_shortcode_id=”221145″][vc_column width=”3/12″][/vc_column][vc_column column_width_percent=”100″ gutter_size=”3″ style=”light” overlay_alpha=”50″ shift_x=”0″ shift_y=”0″ shift_y_down=”0″ z_index=”0″ medium_width=”0″ mobile_width=”0″ width=”6/12″ uncode_shortcode_id=”771324″][vc_custom_heading heading_semantic=”h3″ text_size=”h3″ uncode_shortcode_id=”168375″]3. Curate meaningful landing pages of your collections and products[/vc_custom_heading][vc_custom_heading heading_semantic=”h4″ text_size=”h4″ uncode_shortcode_id=”417197″]What to do[/vc_custom_heading][vc_column_text uncode_shortcode_id=”171218″]

  • Utilise your your skills and group products and collections for rooms and trends
  • This will help your customers find products they might not be looking for but ina  well throughout way
  • ‘Get/shop the look’ on Collection and product pages

[/vc_column_text][vc_custom_heading heading_semantic=”h4″ text_size=”h4″ uncode_shortcode_id=”205611″]Why it is important[/vc_custom_heading][vc_column_text uncode_shortcode_id=”944556″]Chances are you have a lot of products. Use your knowledge and expertise to curate bestseller collections. Group colours, finishing, stylings and trends to make it easy for users to find associated products that would otherwise lay in a separate collection. Enable users to add to the basket from the landing page for the win![/vc_column_text][/vc_column][vc_column width=”3/12″][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row row_height_percent=”0″ override_padding=”yes” h_padding=”2″ top_padding=”5″ bottom_padding=”2″ overlay_alpha=”50″ gutter_size=”3″ column_width_percent=”100″ shift_y=”0″ z_index=”0″ changer_back_color=”yes” uncode_shortcode_id=”221145″][vc_column width=”3/12″][/vc_column][vc_column column_width_percent=”100″ gutter_size=”3″ style=”light” overlay_alpha=”50″ shift_x=”0″ shift_y=”0″ shift_y_down=”0″ z_index=”0″ medium_width=”0″ mobile_width=”0″ width=”6/12″ uncode_shortcode_id=”771324″][vc_custom_heading heading_semantic=”h3″ text_size=”h3″ uncode_shortcode_id=”536660″]4. Collect and showcase User-Generated Content (UGC)[/vc_custom_heading][vc_custom_heading heading_semantic=”h4″ text_size=”h4″ uncode_shortcode_id=”417197″]What to do[/vc_custom_heading][vc_column_text uncode_shortcode_id=”119855″]

  • Create a section on the product page EG ‘As seen on Instagram’ so customers can see your products in real environments from happy customers.
  • Encourage customers to share content. This could be through Socials or email marketing and you could offer a reward/gift to entice more content.

[/vc_column_text][vc_custom_heading heading_semantic=”h4″ text_size=”h4″ uncode_shortcode_id=”205611″]Why it is important[/vc_custom_heading][vc_column_text uncode_shortcode_id=”130295″]Lots of brands struggle to generate images and videos that stand out from their competitors. Prioritising UGC can help because;

  • More relatable to customers and helps build trust seeing real products in real places with real people.
  • More of an authentic way to ensure diversity, rather than handpicking models/influencers.
  • Minimises costs.


Source: Noso, 2023

Creating a community feel is a great way of getting customers to buy into your brand and go onto the next step in the journey. That might be revisiting the website, signing up to socials or signing up to your newsletter. Having engaged customers in turn helps new users to convert in customers.

This approach also helps you to create great unique content which is great for SEO and helps visibility on SERPs (search engine result pages).

Taking the user-generated content a step further you could utilise a customer gallery and link products to the images. 

Reference: https://www.nosto.com/blog/new-research-brands-prefer-ugc-for-diversity/[/vc_column_text][vc_custom_heading heading_semantic=”h4″ text_size=”h4″ uncode_shortcode_id=”749073″]Examples[/vc_custom_heading][vc_column_text uncode_shortcode_id=”167886″]The Ikea Customer Gallery is a section which is used through the site on the homepage, collections and product pages. It allows user generated content to be linked with products, so the user can purchase all the products used in that single UGC image.[/vc_column_text][/vc_column][vc_column width=”3/12″][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row row_height_percent=”0″ override_padding=”yes” h_padding=”2″ top_padding=”2″ bottom_padding=”2″ overlay_alpha=”50″ gutter_size=”3″ column_width_percent=”100″ shift_y=”0″ z_index=”0″ changer_back_color=”yes” uncode_shortcode_id=”840521″][vc_column width=”3/12″][/vc_column][vc_column width=”6/12″][vc_single_image media=”2996″ media_width_percent=”100″ advanced_videos=”yes” mobile_videos=”autoplay” uncode_shortcode_id=”150210″][/vc_column][vc_column width=”3/12″][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row row_height_percent=”0″ override_padding=”yes” h_padding=”2″ top_padding=”5″ bottom_padding=”2″ overlay_alpha=”50″ gutter_size=”3″ column_width_percent=”100″ shift_y=”0″ z_index=”0″ changer_back_color=”yes” uncode_shortcode_id=”221145″][vc_column width=”3/12″][/vc_column][vc_column column_width_percent=”100″ gutter_size=”3″ style=”light” overlay_alpha=”50″ shift_x=”0″ shift_y=”0″ shift_y_down=”0″ z_index=”0″ medium_width=”0″ mobile_width=”0″ width=”6/12″ uncode_shortcode_id=”771324″][vc_custom_heading heading_semantic=”h3″ text_size=”h3″ uncode_shortcode_id=”176904″]5. Build Trust indicators[/vc_custom_heading][vc_custom_heading heading_semantic=”h4″ text_size=”h4″ uncode_shortcode_id=”417197″]What to do[/vc_custom_heading][vc_column_text uncode_shortcode_id=”118918″]

  • Hero your reviews and start gathering reviews with customer photos to help build trust.
  • Show Third-party endorsements.
  • Make Returns & Guarantees easy to find.
  • Think if Trustpilot is right for you.

[/vc_column_text][vc_custom_heading heading_semantic=”h4″ text_size=”h4″ uncode_shortcode_id=”205611″]Why it is important[/vc_custom_heading][vc_column_text uncode_shortcode_id=”955141″]Genuine reviews and product ratings build trust in your products and your brand. Customers are more likely to trust what their peers say over marketing claims.

But trust doesn’t end with customer reviews. Endorsements from known organisations can help with your brand’s credibility. Also enabling Trustpilot widgets is a great way to gain trust without having to say anything.

Lastly, trust and peace of mind about a purchase can play a huge part in converting a user to a customer. Letting users know the policies on delivery and returns can play a huge part in converting potential customers. Try to not hide these bits of information. Having icons near the add to cart button or price has always worked well as the user doesn’t have to go searching, it is always in a predominant part and helps with scan readers.[/vc_column_text][vc_custom_heading heading_semantic=”h4″ text_size=”h4″ uncode_shortcode_id=”749073″]Examples[/vc_custom_heading][vc_column_text uncode_shortcode_id=”148217″]Nkuku bring in their review rating into the stick add to cart on mobile which is a great touch, this is even clickable which anchors links to the review section. [/vc_column_text][/vc_column][vc_column width=”3/12″][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row row_height_percent=”0″ override_padding=”yes” h_padding=”2″ top_padding=”2″ bottom_padding=”2″ overlay_alpha=”50″ gutter_size=”3″ column_width_percent=”100″ shift_y=”0″ z_index=”0″ changer_back_color=”yes” uncode_shortcode_id=”840521″][vc_column width=”3/12″][/vc_column][vc_column width=”6/12″][vc_single_image media=”2997″ media_width_percent=”100″ advanced_videos=”yes” mobile_videos=”autoplay” uncode_shortcode_id=”776831″][/vc_column][vc_column width=”3/12″][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row row_height_percent=”0″ override_padding=”yes” h_padding=”2″ top_padding=”5″ bottom_padding=”2″ overlay_alpha=”50″ gutter_size=”3″ column_width_percent=”100″ shift_y=”0″ z_index=”0″ changer_back_color=”yes” uncode_shortcode_id=”221145″][vc_column width=”3/12″][/vc_column][vc_column column_width_percent=”100″ gutter_size=”3″ style=”light” overlay_alpha=”50″ shift_x=”0″ shift_y=”0″ shift_y_down=”0″ z_index=”0″ medium_width=”0″ mobile_width=”0″ width=”6/12″ uncode_shortcode_id=”771324″][vc_custom_heading heading_semantic=”h3″ text_size=”h3″ uncode_shortcode_id=”284264″]6.   • Put your trust indicators high up on every page. Not just on the homepage
  • Focus on benefits over features
  • Upsell and link related products and blog content

[/vc_column_text][vc_custom_heading heading_semantic=”h4″ text_size=”h4″ uncode_shortcode_id=”205611″]Why it is important[/vc_custom_heading][vc_column_text uncode_shortcode_id=”158896″]Not every user will come from the homepage, some organic users will arrive to a product page via a search engine result page (SERP’s). And may miss out on important messaging or trust indicators that could help convert.

On product pages when you focus on benefits, you’re informing potential customers how your product or can make their lives better. This is much more compelling than just simply listing features. [/vc_column_text][vc_custom_heading heading_semantic=”h4″ text_size=”h4″ uncode_shortcode_id=”749073″]Examples[/vc_custom_heading][vc_column_text uncode_shortcode_id=”137421″]Rockett St George do a great job of having their product pages as content rich landing pages.
